sources.title: Anthony Davison and David Hinkley, Bootstrap Methods and Their Application (1997), Chapter 2 §2.5
sources.locator: Full available 60-page publisher preview, Chapter 2 §2.5 Reducing Error, printed pp. 31–36: statistical error (§2.5.1) and simulation error (§2.5.2).

contents.name: Chapter 2 §2.5 opening distinction between statistical error from estimating the data law and simulation error from finite resampling
§2.5.1 Statistical error: replacing the underlying distribution by its data-based estimate
§2.5.2 Simulation error: empirical estimates from independent resampling replications vary around their exact conditional targets
Other bootstrap confidence-limit, pivotality, and asymptotic-validity discussions in Chapter 2
contents.reason: This error-ledger pair makes no claim that a bootstrap approximation is asymptotically valid or that a finite-replicate confidence interval has nominal coverage.

sources.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Book: The Quasi-Monte Carlo Parts (2019), Chapter 17 Randomized quasi-Monte Carlo
sources.locator: Full 152-page author PDF, Chapter 17 §17.1 printed pp. 89–92, §17.4 pp. 97–100, and Chapter end notes pp. 132–134.

contents.name: Chapter 17 introduction and §17.1: individual uniform marginals give an unbiased randomized rule; independent full-rule replications yield the variance estimate for the replicate mean
§17.1 and §17.4: small replicate counts can give poor variance estimates or interval coverage when replicate distributions are skewed
Chapter end notes: replicate-based CLT and bootstrap-t intervals carry moment, distribution, and finite-R qualifications
Construction-specific scrambled-net rates, discrepancy bounds, and smooth-integrand conditions elsewhere in Chapter 17
contents.reason: This pair does not claim an RQMC convergence rate or a general accuracy bound for a deterministic or randomized quadrature construction.
